newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASEAN meeting to bolster cooperation on AIDS.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN meeting to bolster cooperation on AIDS.

text.p: An ASEAN task force on AIDS will begin a three-day meeting in Singapore on Tuesday to boost cooperation at a time when Asia is poised to overtake Africa as the continent most highly infected by the killer disease.

"These meetings enable the exchange of information and experiences on national campaign(s) against AIDS and cooperation in medical research on AIDS and its social, cultural and economic aspects," Singapore's Health Ministry said in a statement.

"The meeting will also examine the development of HIV/AIDS education and awareness and the strengthening of collaboration between government organisations, NGOs (non-government organisations) and the private sector," it added.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) links Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
As of the end of 1995, a United Nations agency estimated that some 20.1 million adults worldwide were infected with the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), which causes AIDS.
It said that while Africa remained the worst-hit continent, a looming Asian epidemic could easily dwarf what is happening there.
A likely focus of the meeting may be the report of health officials from Thailand, the most heavily-infected country in Southeast Asia.
Nearly one million people in Thailand have been infected with HIV although an aggressive campaign to promote the use of condoms has trimmed the rate of infection.

A study by Johns Hopkins University in the United States said increased condom use in Thailand had led to a dramatic decline in the rate of sexually-transmitted diseases among men to 15.7 percent in 1995 from 42.2 percent in 1991.
The proportion of Thai men who had sex with a prostitute fell to 61 percent in 1995 against 92.5 percent a few years ago.
Despite the anti-AIDS campaign in Thailand, up to four million people may be infected by 2000, health activists there have said.
Only a few hundred people in the Philippines are officially reported to be infected, but analysts believe up to 30,000 Filipinos carry the virus.
In Indonesia, the region's most populous country with nearly 200 million people, at least 303 people are known to be infected with the virus and a further 104 have full-blown AIDS.
Vietnam has more than 3,400 people infected with the virus with about 200 having full-blown AIDS.
In Malaysia, about 14,000 people have the virus.
Health activists have warned that Asian countries reluctant to talk about sex because of cultural taboos may get hit with an epidemic by the turn of the century.
